hist.title: SBSeg History · Timeline, eras and archive figures
hist.metaDesc: History of the Brazilian Cybersecurity Symposium (SBSeg): timeline of the editions, the five eras of the event, institutional milestones and statistics computed from the archive itself (host cities, chairs, keynote speakers and awards).
hist.lead: The trajectory of the Brazilian Cybersecurity Symposium told through what this archive preserves: the host cities, the people who chaired each edition, the invited speakers and the awards. Everything on this page is computed from the archive itself, and every figure links to the page where the underlying data can be checked one by one.
hist.numbersNote: Counts computed from this archive, not from the full history of the symposium. They are recalculated automatically whenever a new edition is catalogued.
hist.erasNote: A reading of the event's history through its format, its governance and its reach. The first period predates what this archive preserves and rests on public SBC records.
hist.era1H: Origins: a workshop inside another event
hist.era1P: The Brazilian security community first gathered in a satellite workshop held alongside the Brazilian Symposium on Computer Networks. There were only a few sessions per year, but enough to reveal a recurring audience and the demand for a forum of its own. Those first editions established the habit of bringing cryptography, network security and systems security together in the same room, a combination that would become the event's signature.
hist.era1Ev: Period predating the archive. Source: public SBC records.
hist.era2P: The event gains standing of its own and is renamed the Brazilian Symposium on Information and Computer Systems Security, with its own call for papers, program committee and proceedings. The 2008 edition, in Gramado, is the oldest preserved here and already shows the format that would hold for years: a main track, four international keynote talks and associated workshops, among them the undergraduate research workshop, which starts in this period and is the longest-running sub-event recorded in this archive.
hist.era2Ev: Archive evidence: SBSeg 2008 (Gramado, UFRGS), 4 invited speakers.
hist.era3H: Travelling the country, and sub-events multiply
hist.era3P: The symposium moves across the country and reaches all five regions: Brasília, Curitiba, Manaus, Belo Horizonte, Florianópolis, Niterói, Natal and São Paulo host consecutive editions. The program stops being a single track and comes to hold specialised workshops on identity management, computer forensics, regulation and certification, and electoral technology, alongside the Tools Session. The 2019 edition is the most diverse of the period: nine distinct tracks and sub-events granted awards, including the event's first hackathon, a mark only surpassed in 2025.
hist.era3Ev: Archive evidence: 9 awarded sub-events in 2019, against 2 in 2017.
hist.era4P: The pandemic breaks the sequence of in-person meetings. The editions nominally hosted in Petrópolis and Belém take place remotely, and the archive itself keeps a trace of it: 2020 is the only catalogued edition with no host institution on record, and the only one whose official site lived on an SBC domain rather than a university's. The 2022 edition, in Santa Maria, marks the return and restores the rotation between regions.
hist.era4Ev: Archive evidence: SBSeg 2020 with no host institution and its site on an SBC domain.
hist.era5P: The main track is explicitly split into Systems and Cryptography, and artifact evaluation enters the program: first by recognising the reviewers, then through a dedicated committee that grants reproducibility badges to papers. In 2025 comes the change of name, from Information and Computer Systems Security to Cybersecurity, together with the renaming of the SBC special commission to CESeg. That same edition introduces a new set of recognitions, among them the test of time award and those for social impact, internationalisation and cooperation.
hist.era5Ev: Archive evidence: artifact badges in 2024; 13 awarded categories in 2025.
hist.timelineNote: One entry per preserved edition, with host city, host institution and the recorded chairing team. Years still lacking a preserved copy are marked as gaps.
hist.timelineJs: The timeline is built from the archive's list of editions. Enable JavaScript to see it, or browse the grid of editions and the organizers page.
hist.tlGap: edition with no preserved copy in this archive
hist.marcosNote: Dated turning points in the shape of the event. Several sub-event debut years are inferred from the ordinal numbering recorded in the preserved award lists, for instance the 8th Tools Session in 2024, which places the first one in 2017.
hist.m2007: First edition of the Undergraduate Research Workshop (WTICG)Inferred: 18th edition held in 2024.
hist.m2008: Oldest edition preserved in this archive: Gramado, at the UFRGS Institute of InformaticsComplete static copy of the original site.
hist.m2011: First edition of the Digital Identity Management Workshop (WGID)Inferred: 9th edition held in 2019.
hist.m2012: First edition of the Computer Forensics Workshop (WFC)Inferred: 8th edition held in 2019.
hist.m2015: First edition of the Workshop on Regulation, Conformity Assessment and Security Certification (WRAC+)Inferred: 5th edition held in 2019.
hist.m2016: First edition of the Electoral Technology Workshop (WTE)Inferred: 4th edition held in 2019.
hist.m2017: First edition of the Tools SessionInferred: 8th edition held in 2024.
hist.m2019: The symposium's first hackathon and the most diverse program up to that point, with nine awarded tracks and sub-eventsAlso the year of the CESeg Distinction Award.
hist.m2020: Remote editions, in 2020 and 2021, interrupt the in-person rotationNominal hosts: Petrópolis and Belém.
hist.m2023: Main track split between Cryptography and Systems Security, and first recognition of artifact reviewersAlso the year of the best reviewer award.
hist.m2024: The Artifact Technical Committee begins granting reproducibility badges to papersEight artifacts distinguished in the first round.
hist.m2025: The event is renamed the Brazilian Cybersecurity Symposium and the SBC special commission becomes CESeg; the test of time, social impact, internationalisation and cooperation awards debutThirteen awarded categories, the highest in the archive.
hist.geoNote: The host cities preserved in this archive and the year each region of the country first appears in the coverage. Editions before 2008 are not covered.
hist.rankNote: Institutions with the most participations in the general chairing or the program committee chairing, counted once per person per edition. It measures organising work, not scientific output.
hist.gapsSubH: This history is incomplete, and that is on purpose
hist.gapsP: The archive preserves what it has been possible to recover so far. The gaps below are known and remain open. If you chaired, attended or kept material from any of these editions, any record helps: pages from the original site, the program, photos, award lists, posters or the composition of the chairing teams.
hist.gap1: Editions before 2008, including the entire workshop period
hist.gap2: The 2009 and 2010 editions, with no preserved copy
hist.gap4: Chairing teams of the 2011 and 2015 editions
hist.gapsContact: Contributions can be sent to CESeg or as a change proposal in the repository of this archive.
hist.note: The figures on this page are computed over the contents of this archive, not over the full history of the symposium, which is larger than the material recovered so far. Sub-event debut dates marked as inferred come from the ordinal numbering stated in the preserved award lists themselves. Corrections are welcome.
hist.footer: Archive page · CESeg / SBC. Data computed from editions, organizers, speakers and awards.

home.title: SBSeg: Brazilian Symposium on Cybersecurity · Historical archive
home.metaDesc: Historical archive and quick-access hub for the editions of SBSeg, the Brazilian Symposium on Cybersecurity (CESeg/SBC): preserved static copies, organizers, speakers, sponsors, awards, photos and even award certificates.
home.eyebrow: Special Committee on Cybersecurity (CESeg) · Brazilian Computer Society (SBC)
home.lead: SBSeg is Brazil's leading national research forum on information security and cybersecurity. This site brings together the event's historical archive, with preserved static copies of each edition that stay accessible here even when the original website goes offline, and also works as a quick-access hub for each edition's information: organizers, speakers, sponsors, awards and photo galleries. It even gathers award certificates, some of which were not available even on the edition's original website.
home.renameEventOld: Brazilian Symposium on Information and Computer Systems Security
home.renameCommOld: Special Committee on Information and Computer Systems Security
home.renameNote: Up to the 2024 edition the longer name was in use; from 2025 the current, official and more concise name took effect. The acronyms SBSeg and CESeg were kept.
home.mapCaption: 17 editions across 16 host cities all over Brazil. Hover (or tap) a dot to see the city, the host institution and the year of each edition; click to jump to the edition's card.
home.mapAria: Map of Brazil with the host cities of the SBSeg editions
home.cardOrgP: General Chairs and Program Committee Chairs (main track) of each edition.
home.cardSpeakersP: Invited keynote speakers from previous editions, with affiliation and links.
home.cardAwardsP: Award-winning papers by edition, across all categories and sub-events.
home.cardPhotosP: Thumbnails and links to each edition's photo albums (website, Google Drive and social media).
home.cardSponsorsP: Sponsors and supporters across the editions, organized by tier.
home.archiveNote: Several editions have a preserved static copy in this project, which stays accessible here even if the original site goes down. Where a copy exists, the Static copy button appears on the edition card; the Original site button points to the live site (when still available).

speakers.title: Speakers of the SBSeg Editions
speakers.lead: A compilation of the invited keynote speakers from previous editions of the Brazilian Symposium on Cybersecurity (SBSeg). Includes name, affiliation and academic/professional links when available.
speakers.note: Data compiled from the Previous Editions page of SBSeg 2025 and from the program/speaker pages of each edition (including archived sites). The 2011 and 2015 editions are still pending, as no detailed program is available on the archived sites, and will be added together with the speakers' photos in a future stage.

awards.title: Awards of the SBSeg Editions
awards.lead: List of the award-winning papers in each edition of the Brazilian Symposium on Cybersecurity, organized by sub-event and award category. Current coverage: 139 awards in the editions with an available source.
awards.note: Editions included so far: 2025, 2024, 2023, 2022, 2019, 2017, 2014 and 2012 (those with an accessible awards list). The remaining editions will be added as the sources are located. The 2022 list is preliminary and not yet confirmed against the official certificates.
